new_findings.claim: New behaviour introduced by the P0 fix: because 'NOT json_valid(d.metadata_json)' puts unparseable rows back into the LIMIT window, a period query can be SHADOWED by a blocked non-matching row - the very shadowing the clause's own comment says the advisory filter exists to prevent ('an advisory json_extract filter narrows the slice so a 100-cap cannot shadow an older-period request'). Neither the disposition table nor package doc section 7 mentions this side effect.
new_findings.counter_evidence: Command: 'python %TEMP%\b05v\probe_shadow.py %TEMP%\b05v\head %TEMP%\b05v\scratch' on the copy, two real annual reports in one catalog: Z (published_date 2026-02-20, later) corrupted to '{not json' and A (published_date 2026-01-10) left well-formed with acquisition.fiscal_year=2025. Observed: fiscal_year=2025 limit=100 -> [('Z-acme-2025','blocked'), ('A-acme-2025','ok')]; limit=2 -> same; limit=1 -> [('Z-acme-2025','blocked')] - the genuine 2025 match is omitted from the 2025 request. Impact today is limited: the resolver calls query_filing_candidates without fiscal_year (resolver.py:1314-1318 passes only document_kind / source_statuses / limit=1000, as B-VR05M-01's residual already noted), so no in-package caller reaches the filtered variant.
new_findings.required_fix: Either document the trade-off explicitly in the package doc and the SQL comment (blocked rows are kept and can occupy the cap), or rank/partition malformed rows so the period match is never displaced (e.g. apply the period predicate to well-formed rows and append the unparseable remainder after the matched slice), and pin whichever behaviour is chosen with a case.
